interface.title: Aether: NetCDF Explorer
interface.field: Climate and earth-system science (gridded geospatial time series)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory data analysis and quick-look checks of model or reanalysis output
interface.what_it_is_for: Load a NetCDF file by its path, map a variable over lat/lon through time, and click a cell or drag a box to get its timeseries, anomalies, smoothing, trend statistics and annual cycle.

data.note: I typed /work/app/data/sample.nc into 'NetCDF File Path' and pressed Load File. It holds the variable tas (K, Near-Surface Air Temperature) on time(24 monthly steps, 2015-01 to 2016-12) × lat(10) × lon(12), covering about 20–60N and -130 to -60E. The global attributes say it is synthetic demo data. There is no coastline overlay.

screens_never_reached: 4th/5th Dimension selectors: the sample file has only time, lat and lon, so these only offered None
Coastline overlay on the map: it is patched out because the server has no network to download Natural Earth shapefiles
not_done: Did not find the injected hot outlier or the NaN cell. I checked Map Stats at times 0, 1, 5, 7, 19 and 23 and none showed an extreme max, and I did not step through every time index, so handling of missing data and outliers was not tested.
The default colour scaling is robust (1st–99th percentile, get_robust_min_max in the code, per the reviewer); the run only set Min/Max by hand and never saw the default range applied to an outlier.

Did not choose a date range for trend fitting through 'Select Dates': that control takes only one date and just moves the map's time step. Choosing a sub-period was done with the draggable endpoints instead.

Known failure: setting X Dimension = time with Y = lat (a time–latitude view) failed with 'Error updating plot: object of type numpy.datetime64 has no len()' (screens/024.webp); choosing lon again restored the map (screens/025.webp).

The Annual Cycle is the monthly mean of the selected series (update_cycles in aether.py, per the reviewer's code reading), so it does follow the selection. Its bars use a 0–300 axis, so month-to-month differences are hard to see and the point and area bars looked about the same.
The OLS→Theil-Sen header change (0.1565 to 0.1178) was not isolated: the Anomalies tab was also active on screens/007.webp, so the estimator's own effect on the header trend was not measured.
Only one variable (tas) was in the file, so I could not try switching variables.
Did not try the Save buttons on the timeseries, profile or annual-cycle plots, or the wheel-zoom and pan tools beyond accidental wheel zooming of the timeseries (screens/025.webp).

open_fixes: Rerun the check with the path /work/app/data/sample.nc: every not_confirmed reflects the checker failing to load a file (it tried /work/data/sample.nc and others), and only a new replay can change those statuses.
Explore with a multi-variable, 4-D or 5-D NetCDF file to cover variable switching and the 4th/5th Dimension slicing selectors; the 3-D single-variable sample could not reach them.
Step through every time index (or use a file with a known outlier and NaN) to test the default robust colour range and missing-data handling, which this run never observed.
Toggle OLS/Theil-Sen alone on one tab to measure the estimator's own effect on the header trend; the recorded screens mix it with a tab change.
